item.content: {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=causal+states+coarse+graining+physical+memory+prediction&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"A mathematical theory of redox biology\", \"abstract\": null, \"doi\": null, \"pmid\": \"PMC13641906\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13641906\", \"source\": \"PMC\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13641906/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13641906/pdf/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13641906\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13641906?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"What is emergence, after all?\", \"abstract\": \"The term emergence is increasingly used across scientific disciplines to describe phenomena that arise from interactions among a system's components but cannot be readily inferred by examining those components in isolation. While often invoked to explain higher-level behaviors-such as flocking, synchronization, or collective intelligence-the term is frequently used without precision, sometimes giving rise to ambiguity or even mystique. In this perspective paper, I clarify the scientific meaning of emergence as a measurable and physically grounded phenomenon. Through concrete examples-such as temperature, magnetism, and herd immunity in social networks-I review how collective behavior can arise from local interactions that are constrained by global boundaries. By refining the concept of emergence, it is possible to gain a clearer and more grounded understanding of complex systems. My goal is to show that emergence, when properly framed, offers not mysticism, but rather insight.\", \"doi\": \"10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag010\", \"pmid\": \"41684806\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC12893386\", \"source\": \"MED\",…
